topics.topic: Behavior when a listed path is replaced by another regular file before opening or placement
questions: If the listed file is renamed but another regular file appears at the same listed path before it is opened, must placement reject the identity change with `unreadable_file`, process the replacement using the original name judgement, or reclassify the replacement?
If the listed file is renamed but another regular file appears at the same listed path before it is opened, must placement reject the stale observation or may it read and place the replacement?
What happens when the listed file is renamed away but another regular file occupies the listed path before placement reads it, especially when the replacement has the same content?

judgement.why: P4 already decides replacement at the listed path: placement uses the operation’s scan and source-content hash, accepts replacement bytes matching the requested hash, and otherwise reports `source_changed`.

precedent.topic: How placement handles a path that reappears after observation and detects a past rename
quotes: A placement is identified by the project and the SHA-256 of the source content (R0-10).

Inside the call the folder is scanned once. A requested source with no placement that this scan
does not report as `ready` fails with `not_ready_or_absent`. A source reported `ready` whose
bytes no longer have the requested hash when it is read for placing fails with `source_changed`.

A replaced source is a new photo. The earlier placement, its stored image and its mark stay.
   Removing a source changes no placement (R0-10).
precedent.why: Placement uses the operation’s scan and source-content hash rather than historical file identity, so a currently ready path containing the requested bytes may be placed without detecting an earlier rename.

topics.topic: Whether existing placement replay takes precedence over INV-18 unreadable-file failures
questions: Is the required failure when placing a conflict copy by hash limited to content that has no existing placement, while already placed content must replay?
Must the disappearing-ordinary-file failure test start without an existing placement, or does `unreadable_file` override replay when that content was already placed?

judgement.why: P1 already decides that existing-placement replay takes precedence regardless of the current source name, while conflict-copy and unreadable-file failures apply only when a new placement must read a source.

precedent.topic: Whether an existing placement replays instead of renamed-file or conflict-copy failure
quotes: content that already has a placement replays under A3 rule 2 whatever name it has now.

Placing an existing placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the current
   `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, even when the source file has left the
   folder.
